best_architecture: Local-Claw should manage context as a three-tier MemGPT-style virtual-memory hierarchy mapped directly onto its existing three-store stack, with a hybrid-RAG retrieval pipeline feeding the in-context window and a token-budget allocator as the central control loop. (1) WORKING TIER = the live Gemma context window backed by a Redis cache. It holds the system prompt, agent-self-editable core memory blocks (persona, current goal/plan, user preferences), the recent turns verbatim (sliding window), and the retrieved/compressed context assembled for the current step. Redis stores the durable core-memory blocks and recent-turn buffer so working state survives a context-window reset. (2) SEMANTIC/ARCHIVAL TIER = Chroma vector store holding facts, distilled summaries, and documents (cold knowledge retrieved on demand). (3) EPISODIC TIER = MongoDB full session history, every raw message persisted chronologically and never compressed. The agent actively pages data between tiers with explicit MemGPT-style tool calls (core_memory_append, core_memory_replace, archival_memory_insert, archival_memory_search, conversation_search) rather than receiving a fixed passive context. RETRIEVAL is hybrid RAG, not vector-only: run BM25 lexical (rank_bm25) and Chroma dense vector search in parallel, fuse with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60), then apply a cross-encoder reranker (FlagReranker / bge-reranker-v2-m3) over the fused top ~50 to select the final 5-10 chunks. Hybrid+rerank materially beats dense-only for coding work because BM25 catches exact identifiers, error codes, and file paths that embeddings miss. COMPRESSION uses two complementary techniques: rolling summary buffering (recent turns verbatim + an LLM-maintained running summary of older turns) for conversation history, and Chain-of-Density iterative entity-densification at fixed length for high-value artifacts (specs, key files, session summaries). Raw turns always remain recoverable from the MongoDB episodic tier, so compression is never lossy at the source. TOKEN BUDGETING is the defining control loop: partition the fixed Gemma window into explicit named sub-budgets each step (system+core memory, sliding window of recent turns, retrieved RAG, summary buffer, and a completion reserve), and never exceed the effective limit. Token counting MUST use the native Gemma HuggingFace AutoTokenizer (SentencePiece), NOT tiktoken, because tiktoken's GPT BPE vocabulary miscounts Gemma tokens (errors of 30%+ on code-heavy prompts). The most important design decision is that eviction/compression is a budget-constrained allocation problem solved every step against remaining capacity and the current goal, not a one-shot truncation when the window happens to overflow.
reference_papers: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems (Packer et al., 2023) - arXiv:2310.08560. Foundational paper for tiered/virtual context management. Defines main/working context (RAM) vs recall memory (searchable history) vs archival memory (vector store), agent-managed paging via function calls (core_memory_append, archival_memory_search), and interrupt-driven control flow. Directly maps to Local-Claw's Redis/Chroma/MongoDB tiers; productized as Letta.

Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (Sumers, Yao, Narasimhan, Griffiths, 2023) - arXiv:2309.02427 (TMLR 2024). The CoALA taxonomy: working (short-term, in-context) vs long-term memory (episodic experience, semantic facts, procedural skills) plus the decision cycle propose->evaluate->select->execute. Conceptual basis for separating the working/semantic/episodic tiers.

From Sparse to Dense: GPT-4 Summarization with Chain of Density Prompting (Adams et al., 2023) - arXiv:2309.04269. Iterative summarization that repeatedly injects missing salient entities while holding summary length fixed, raising information density per token. The reference technique for high-retention compression of session summaries and key artifacts.

Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey (Gao et al., 2023) - arXiv:2312.10997. Survey of naive/advanced/modular RAG covering hybrid retrieval, reranking, and query transformation; grounds the hybrid BM25+dense+rerank pipeline for the semantic tier.
Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering (Karpukhin et al., 2020) - arXiv:2004.04906. The dense bi-encoder retrieval foundation underpinning the vector leg of hybrid retrieval.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion outperforms Condorcet and individual Rank Learning Methods (Cormack, Clarke, Buettcher, 2009) - ACM SIGIR 2009, DOI:10.1145/1645953.1646039. The RRF algorithm score(d)=sum 1/(k+rank_r(d)) with default k=60; the standard rank-based way to fuse BM25 and dense results without score normalization.

Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (Liu et al., 2023) - arXiv:2307.03172. Shows models attend best to the start and end of the window and degrade on content buried in the middle; the basis for keeping top-k small, reranking for quality, and position-aware prompt assembly.

Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory (Rasmussen et al., 2025) - arXiv:2501.13956. Bi-temporal (valid-time + transaction-time) knowledge graph (Graphiti) for evolving agent memory; beats MemGPT on DMR (94.8% vs 93.4%) and gains up to 18.5% on LongMemEval with ~90% lower latency. The SOTA upgrade path for the semantic tier.

pitfalls: Using tiktoken for Gemma token budgeting. tiktoken uses OpenAI's GPT BPE vocabulary (cl100k/o200k); it cannot encode Gemma's SentencePiece vocabulary and produces wrong counts - errors of 30%+ on code-heavy prompts (whitespace, indentation, symbols, non-ASCII). Always count with the Gemma HF AutoTokenizer (transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained), or the budget allocator will over- or under-fill the window and trigger silent truncation.

Lost-in-the-middle retrieval. Returning 20 chunks puts the most relevant ones in the middle of the window where Gemma attends worst (arXiv:2307.03172). Keep top-k small and use the cross-encoder reranker to select for QUALITY not QUANTITY (top 5-10), and place the highest-scoring chunks at the head and tail of the prompt, not buried in the middle.

Evicting goal state from the working tier (the Sisyphus Trap). Aggressive compression that drops the current task goal/plan from core memory makes the agent lose track of what it is doing and loop. Pin the goal/plan in a protected core-memory block in Redis that compression never evicts; only summarize/evict conversational filler.

Vector-only retrieval for code. Dense embeddings miss exact variable names, error codes (e.g. ECONNREFUSED), and file paths. BM25 lexical retrieval is an essential complement for the code-heavy episodic/semantic memory; never ship vector-only retrieval for a coding agent.

No memory dedup. On retries the same message gets re-embedded and re-inserted, creating duplicate vectors that inflate similarity scores and crowd retrieval results with the same content. Deduplicate on a content hash before upsert into Chroma, and on retry update-in-place rather than insert.

Summary buffer too aggressive. Summarizing recent turns too eagerly destroys the step-by-step reasoning the agent needs to avoid repeating mistakes (e.g. which fix it already tried). Keep a generous verbatim recent-turn window; only compress turns older than the recent window, and re-summarize from the MongoDB episodic source when fidelity matters.

Core-memory blocks growing unbounded. A self-edit/append tool with no cap lets core memory grow until it fills the window and squeezes out retrieved context and recent turns. Enforce per-block and total core-memory caps; require core_memory_replace (rewrite) instead of endless append, and warn/compact when a block nears its cap.

Consolidation on the hot path. Blocking on Chroma upsert / embedding during every agent step adds latency to each turn. Episodic-to-semantic consolidation (embedding, summarizing, vector upsert) must run async off the hot path (motor writes + a background consolidation worker), so the agent step only reads, never blocks on a write.

    And a hybrid retriever combining BM25 and Chroma dense vectors fused with RRF and reranked by a cross-encoder

    Then BM25 returns the exact entry containing "ECONNREFUSED" in its top results
    And the dense-vector leg returns semantically similar but less relevant entries
    And RRF fusion (k=60) ranks the exact lexical match above the merely-similar results
    And the cross-encoder rerank keeps the exact error entry in the final top 5

  Scenario: Token budget enforcement leaves a completion reserve
    Given a Gemma 4 context budget of 8192 tokens
    When the context builder assembles system prompt, core memory, recent turns, retrieved RAG, and summary buffer
    Then the total token count measured by the Gemma AutoTokenizer never exceeds 7500
    And the remaining tokens are reserved for the model completion
    And if a tier would overflow the budget, only that tier is compressed or trimmed

  Scenario: Core-memory self-edit survives a context-window reset
    Given the agent discovers a user preference during a session
    When the agent calls the core_memory_append tool with that preference
    Then the new entry is persisted to the Redis working-tier store
    And after the context window is reset and rebuilt
    Then the persisted preference is present in core memory again

  Scenario: Chain-of-Density compression densifies at fixed length
    Given a 2000-word session summary in the episodic tier
    When the Chain-of-Density skill is applied for 3 iterations
    Then the output summary is 200 words or fewer
    And each iteration adds previously-missing salient entities while holding the length fixed
    And the final summary has higher entity density than the first iteration
optimal_implementation:
Implement a single ContextManager facade over the three tiers, a hybrid retriever, a Gemma-aware token counter, and an async consolidation worker.

1) Token counting (Gemma SentencePiece, NOT tiktoken):
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
_tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("google/gemma-2-9b-it")  # match deployed Gemma
def token_count(text: str) -> int:
    return len(_tok.encode(text, add_special_tokens=False))
```

2) Context builder with explicit sub-budgets and completion reserve:
```python
class TokenBudgetedContext(BaseModel):
    system_prompt: str
    core_memory: str
    recent_turns: str
    retrieved_context: str
    summary_buffer: str
    total_tokens: int

class ContextManager:
    def __init__(self, redis, chroma, mongo, retriever, llm):
        self.redis=redis; self.chroma=chroma; self.mongo=mongo
        self.retriever=retriever; self.llm=llm

    def build_context(self, session_id, current_task, max_tokens=8192):
        reserve = int(max_tokens * 0.10)            # completion reserve
        budget  = max_tokens - reserve              # ~7500 for 8192
        sys = SYSTEM_PROMPT
        core = self.redis.get(f"core:{session_id}") or ""   # self-editable, pinned goal
        b_sys = token_count(sys) + token_count(core)
        # retrieved RAG: hybrid + rerank, packed to its share
        rag = self._pack(self.retriever.hybrid_retrieve(current_task),
                         int(budget*0.35))
        # recent turns: sliding window trimmed to its share
        recent = self._trim_recent(session_id, int(budget*0.30))
        summary = self.redis.get(f"summary:{session_id}") or ""
        ctx = TokenBudgetedContext(system_prompt=sys, core_memory=core,
            recent_turns=recent, retrieved_context=rag, summary_buffer=summary,
            total_tokens=0)
        ctx.total_tokens = sum(token_count(x) for x in
            [sys, core, recent, rag, summary])
        assert ctx.total_tokens <= budget, "budget overflow -> compress a tier"
        return ctx
```
Assemble the final prompt with the highest-value content (system+core, then top reranked chunks) at the HEAD and a recap of the goal at the TAIL to counter lost-in-the-middle.

3) Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + Chroma dense -> RRF -> cross-encoder):
```python
from FlagEmbedding import FlagReranker
reranker = FlagReranker("BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3", use_fp16=True)

def rrf(rankings, k=60):
    s={}
    for r in rankings:
        for rank, doc_id in enumerate(r, start=1):
            s[doc_id]=s.get(doc_id,0.0)+1.0/(k+rank)
    return s

def hybrid_retrieve(query, bm25, chroma_coll, top_k=50, final_k=8):
    bm25_ids  = bm25.get_top_n_ids(query, n=top_k)
    dense_ids = chroma_coll.query(query_texts=[query], n_results=top_k)["ids"][0]
    fused = rrf([bm25_ids, dense_ids], k=60)
    shortlist = sorted(fused, key=fused.get, reverse=True)[:top_k]
    docs = load_docs(shortlist)
    scores = reranker.compute_score([[query, d.text] for d in docs])
    ranked = [d for _, d in sorted(zip(scores, docs), key=lambda x: -x[0])]
    return ranked[:final_k]
```

4) Async consolidation worker (off the hot path):
```python
import asyncio
async def consolidation_worker(queue, chroma_coll, embed):
    while True:
        rec = await queue.get()                  # episodic write event
        h = content_hash(rec.text)
        if chroma_coll.get(ids=[h])["ids"]:       # dedup on content hash
            queue.task_done(); continue
        chroma_coll.add(ids=[h], documents=[rec.text],
                        embeddings=[embed(rec.text)], metadatas=[rec.meta])
        queue.task_done()
```
The agent step only enqueues writes (and persists raw turns to MongoDB via motor); embedding + Chroma upsert happen in the worker so each step never blocks on a write.

5) Compression: SummaryBuffer keeps the recent N turns verbatim and maintains a running summary; for high-value artifacts call a Chain-of-Density skill (3-5 passes, add missing salient entities while holding length fixed). Always re-summarize from the MongoDB episodic source when fidelity matters - raw turns are never lost. Enforce per-block and total core-memory caps; pin the current goal/plan in a protected core block that compression cannot evict.
sota_improvements: Bi-temporal memory (Zep/Graphiti, arXiv:2501.13956): track when facts were TRUE (valid time) and when they were LEARNED (transaction time), not just that they were true. Enables as-of-date queries ('what did the agent know about X on day 3') and conflict resolution that invalidates - rather than deletes - superseded facts. Beats MemGPT on DMR and gains up to 18.5% on LongMemEval. Strong upgrade for the Chroma semantic tier.

MemoryOS-style automatic hot/warm/cold tiering: treat Redis as L1 hot, Chroma as L2 warm, MongoDB as L3 cold, with automatic promotion/demotion driven by recency and importance scoring instead of purely manual MemGPT-style paging.

Sparse+dense via SPLADE or ColBERT late-interaction instead of (or alongside) BM25+dense: late-interaction models understand code tokens better than bag-of-words BM25, improving code retrieval precision; ColBERT reranking is a cheaper middle ground than a full cross-encoder.

Adaptive retrieval depth: route top-k by task type - small top-k for short edits, larger top-k for long research/refactor tasks - so the retrieved-context budget scales with how much context the task actually needs.

KV-cache / prefix sharing across agent steps (vLLM automatic prefix caching): cache the shared system prompt + stable core-memory prefix so each agent step gets faster time-to-first-token; pairs well with keeping the stable prefix at the head of the assembled prompt.
